references.text: The verse refers to the practices of the peoples in Canaan that the Israelites were not to imitate, establishing the context for the abominations mentioned in verse 27.
These verses describe how the nations became unclean through their actions and how the land was defiled, directly parallel to the description in verse 27.
Repeats the warning not to follow the customs of the nations that God is driving out, because they did all these things and became abominable to the Lord.
Moses explains that it is because of the wickedness of these nations that God drives them out of the land, not because of Israel's righteousness.
Warns Israel against worshipping God in the same way that the nations worshipped their gods, because they did abominable things which the Lord hates.
Describes how those who practice abominable things are an abomination to the Lord, and this is why God drives out the nations.
Describes how Israel itself began to do the abominations of the nations that the Lord had driven out before them.
King Ahaz walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and practiced the abominations of the nations that the Lord had driven out.
King Manasseh did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, following the abominations of the nations that the Lord had driven out before the children of Israel.
Ezekiel describes how the house of Israel made the land unclean through their conduct and their deeds, like a woman's uncleanness.
